what_was_done: Each of the three restatements is gone, and two more of the same kind that a search found. (1) 'The tool never reads the value of a key variable' is deleted from config/flags.md 'Keys and local runs'; the fact stays in F-KEY's reads cell. (2) Which table a check reads, [flags] before [flags.approved], stays in config/flags.md 'Who writes it' and nowhere else: the header of flag-config-keys.toml now says only that override = true marks a key a person may also write, with a link to config:flags, and 'and wins' is cut from the meaning of flags.enabled. (3) The moved-test rule keeps its reason in feature-flags.md 'Why it is this way' and its rule in the test-writer's duty, F-STATES and F-ON. flag-lifecycle.md 'Delivered off' is cut to a link to the duty and F-STATES, 'Who turns a flag on' names F-ON instead of restating its refusal of a pending test, and step 6 of feature-flags.md no longer restates the move. Also: where a person overrides a member repository's flag values is now only in the row flags.repo.<name> (config/flags.md links to it), and that the spec packet lists overrides is now only in flag-system-choice.md.

Decided: a story removes a flag in one of two ways and says which in flag_change (artifacts/flag.md). remove keeps the behaviour of a value other than the default, which for a release flag is the on behaviour; withdraw keeps the behaviour of the default, so the feature is given up. This replaces 'the request says which behaviour stays', which no program could read. Each duty now fits its checks. Every removal leaves no test that sets the key: the tests of the behaviour that goes and the test of the definition are deleted, and the flag setting is taken out of every other test. remove deletes the off, default and old tests and writes the regression test. withdraw deletes the on tests and every other test that turns the flag on, gives each moved test its own name back and takes the token out of the names of the off and default tests. F-DEFINITION refuses, at the head of either, a test that sets the key or still carries a token of the flag, other than an on test after a remove. A pending test: F-STATES refuses a remove at its red gate while the base report holds a pending test of the flag, and names each, so the story stops before anything is built; flag-lifecycle.md 'Removal' gives the way through (the stories behind the flag provide what the test asserts, which gives it its name back, or the flag is withdrawn). Walking a withdrawal through red showed a second defect of the same clause: nothing the product does with no flag set changes, so no test can fail first and the red gate could never pass. F-STATES now asks a withdrawal for no red test, applies no red share, maps no test to a criterion and says so in its record, and it refuses a moved test of the base report that has not come back. The item flag-removed now also covers which tests the diff deletes and that a test brought back or renamed is unchanged; review-stories checks each flag_change against the request. F-REQUIRE holds both removals to kind fix, F-REMOVE counts either as an open removal, the record is removed after either, and the release packet says which behaviour stays. F4 gains a harness scenario for a withdrawal, and ledger entry D31-1 names the three values.
where: rewrite/spec/tables/flag-duties.toml (story-writer, test-writer, implementer, adversary), rewrite/spec/tables/flag-story-checks.toml (F-STATES, F-DEFINITION, F-ITEMS), rewrite/spec/tables/flag-checks.toml (F-REQUIRE), rewrite/spec/tables/flag-release-checks.toml (F-REMOVE), rewrite/spec/artifacts/flag.md, rewrite/spec/topics/flag-lifecycle.md, rewrite/spec/topics/feature-flags.md, rewrite/spec/commands/gate-red.md and rewrite/spec/workflows/story.md (D31 passages), rewrite/spec/registry.d/d31.toml (F4), rewrite/findings/sources/extra-d31.json (D31-1)

what_was_done: Package F2, when it builds F-ON, widens the description of test_defects in next/plugins/vsdd-factory/schemas/implement-data.schema.json to: tests the builder believes are wrong and may not edit: frozen tests, and existing tests that the green gate's run with a flag on names. The shape (path, test, reason) does not change. The story script's prompt stays as it is, so nothing on the slice path changes; F4's harness scenario runs the moved-test path through that prompt. The design side is settled: the implementer's duty in flag-duties.toml and the D31 passage of workflows/story.md say that such a test travels under test_defects, and F2's delivers text names this entry. It can only be settled in code, because the schema is shipped under next/.

Neither proposed fix was enough alone. A moved test is an existing test, and in a product the factory built its own name already holds the ac<N> of the story that wrote it, so the criteria map would show it under that number whatever criterion the move added or left out. Decided: a moved test is evidence of no criterion. The duty no longer adds a criterion to a moved name, and F-STATES leaves moved tests out of the record's criteria map, so gate demo's table never shows a test of the old behaviour as evidence of the new one. For the tests the story writes itself, F-STATES now reads the story's criteria and refuses a new off or default test that names no criterion, or names one whose text lacks 'flag off'; the duty says the same. So that the rule also holds when a test gets its own name back, a moved name now has one form: the test's own name with __flag_old_<k> or __flag_pending_<k> added. A program can then tell which test a moved test was and when it has come back. F-STATES refuses a new moved test that the base report does not hold, refuses a missing test that the head does not hold as a moved test (this replaces the count of missing tests against moved tests), and treats a test that has come back as neither new nor evidence of a criterion. Which existing test a moved test was is no longer unmeasured; the item flag-off keeps what is a judgment (assertions unchanged, old only where a criterion replaces).

Corrected from the other side, because this task may not edit packaging/build-plan.md. The sweep form of F-CHOICE moved from F5 to F6, the package that builds everything else the sweep job gains. F5 now delivers the planning gates only (vsdd gate spec and vsdd gate plan) and depends on F1 and G5. F6 delivers F-CHOICE as advisory findings in the sweep's spec coherence check, from the module F5 ships, and depends on F5 as well as G7. Step 5 of the build plan ('F5 the planning gates; ... F6 the wave, release and sweep jobs') is therefore right as it stands and needs no edit, and its order F1, F5, F2, F6 already builds F5 before F6. The header of flag-checks.toml names F6 for the sweep form, and the briefs are regenerated.

The design is settled in the spec; the shipped artifact registry (next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/policy/artifacts.toml) and the artifact rule must follow it when package F1 is built, in the same change as D31-1. F1 adds: the stem cell of the [flag] row and the check that a record's path is its key percent-encoded (the id no longer equals the stem); the lock value removed (frozen once a delivered story removes the flag, with flag_change: remove or withdraw); the fourth story key flag_irreversible and the record keys permanent_because and default_because, as artifacts/flag.md gives them; the [deferred-item] writer vsdd checkpoint, with the item named deferred/flag-<stem>.md; and a [toolchain] cap of 12,000 bytes. The spec side is done: artifacts/flag.md states the two format additions, flag-lifecycle.md and state-layout.md use <stem>, and artifacts/toolchain.md states the cap.
